page: Amazon Web Services r8g.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton processors built on the arm64 Neoverse-V2 architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz, with 1 thread per core, backed by 64 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. Hypervisor functions are managed by the AWS Nitro System. The system provides 384.0 GB of memory, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, relying instead on network-attached storage over an established 22 Gbps baseline network interface.

Benchmark data confirms strong multithreaded and memory performance. The instance achieved top-tier throughput in large-block uncached memory benchmarks, recording 404.36 GB/sec in read and 201.11 GB/sec in write operations. In PassMark database operations, it reached 47,285.97, placing it in the top 10% of evaluated hardware. Multithreaded execution is robust, as demonstrated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 23,531.0 and a Clang compilation score of 68,947.0. Single-core results are comparatively modest, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,894.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,706.6 placing it in the middle tier.

From an architectural efficiency perspective, the dedicated arm64 physical core allocation avoids simultaneous multithreading resource contention, yielding consistent high-concurrency throughput. The absence of local disk implies that IO-intensive workloads must account for network volume latency. The r8g.12xlarge is well aligned for memory-bound applications, large in-memory caches, relational database systems, multi-threaded compile farms, and high-throughput static web serving.

Operating under the AWS Nitro System, the instance provides 22 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and operates without local storage or GPUs. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 404 GB/sec read and 201 GB/sec write, coupled with top-tier database operation scores and high multi-core performance, such as a 23,531.0 Geekbench multi-core score.
